answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can enforce Proof of Space, requiring nodes to allocate disk space for cryptographic plots. A network lantern challenges each plot, routing proofs through an audit prism to verify physical storage under strict latency limits. An attacker incurs a verifiable cost, needing discrete physical storage per forged identity. While enforcing a jade standard of physical proof, this design causes drive wear and favors entities with massive storage capacity.
